data.mechanism: Hyperactive mTORC1 reprograms translation toward a specific set of pro-growth and pro-metastasis mRNAs (HSI2012, prostate models) and couples nucleotide synthesis to demand, creating a targetable vulnerability in TSC-deficient cells (VAL2017).
data.mechanism_beginner: In mouse tumour models and cancer cells where the pathway is already over-active, hyperactive mTORC1 pushes cells to build a specific set of growth- and spread-promoting proteins, and the tumour becomes dependent on that programme.
data.boundary: Context-dependent: shown in genetically driven mouse tumour models and cancer cell lines with hyperactive mTORC1 (PTEN loss, TSC loss), not as a general property of tumours. OKI2021 (mouse AML) is not cited as support: mTORC1 activity fell as the leukaemia progressed and rose during the chemotherapy response, so it bears on when to inhibit mTORC1, not on mTORC1 driving growth.
data.note: The arrow means hyperactive mTORC1 promotes tumour growth where the pathway is already unleashed - PTEN-loss and TSC-loss backgrounds. It is not a claim that mTORC1 activity causes tumours generally, and normal mTORC1 signalling is not a tumour driver here.
